subject: Approval needed: contract unwind terms & staged ramp repricing — Cascade Health
messages:
From: Alyssa Grant <alyssa.grant@cascadehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cascadehealth.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract terms — staged ramp + unwind options

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo. Our procurement team needs to review the commercial terms for the pilot + potential enterprise roll. Two items surfaced that will block signature unless we can get clarity: 1) an explicit staged ramp pricing schedule (we need a defined per-month seat/token discount as usage scales up) and 2) an "unwind" / opt-out path for the pilot that doesn't expose us to disproportionate committed costs if the integration proves misaligned.

We are okay with a ramp commitment, but would like either a downhill protection (downsell credits) or a short early-uncoupling fee capped at two months of committed spend. Can Redwood propose exact language so we can circulate with legal?

Attaching our internal procurement checklist for context.

Best,
Alyssa
Senior Procurement Manager
Cascade Health

Attachment: cascade_procurement_checklist.pdf (stub)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Contract terms — staged ramp + unwind options (escalation)

Team — forwarding Cascade's ask. They want: explicit month-by-month ramp discounts + a capped early uncoupling/opt-out that limits their downside.

Key points:
- They are willing to commit to a 6 month pilot (50k tokens/month baseline) with step-up in month 3 and month 5 if adoption is there.
- Proposed opt-out asks for a 2-month cap on termination exposure. Procurement asked for either downsell credit (apply remaining committed value as credit against lower tier) OR a flat fee cap.

I'm requesting:
- Sales + Finance: quick approval on a downsell credit structure vs flat fee. See cost_breakdown.xlsx attached for impact.
- Legal (Laura): please propose two short redline options (A: downsell credit language; B: capped uncoupling fee) we can send back to the customer.

This is time-sensitive — Alyssa said procurement will escalate if we don't respond with proposed language by Monday EOD.

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cascade_contract_draft_v2.pdf (contract draft), cost_breakdown.xlsx (stub)

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract terms — staged ramp + unwind options (escalation)

Sean — quick thoughts after looking at cost_breakdown:
- Option A (downsell credit): For the 6-month pilot commit, we can allow a downsell recapture where any unused committed spend is converted to credit over the following 3 months at the lower rate, up to a maximum of 50% of the remaining committed value. This preserves revenue but gives customer gradual relief.
- Option B (flat uncoupling fee): Cap at 2 months of committed spend (aligns with their ask). Lower friction but higher short-term revenue hit for us if they opt out early.

Finance: the worst-case revenue delta for Option A is ~18% vs baseline; Option B is ~22% in the first quarter of an unwind scenario. See cost_breakdown.xlsx for the scenarios.

Recommend offering Option A as default, and include Option B as a negotiable concession for enterprise-level commitments only. Also suggest compressing ramp milestones to Month 2 and Month 4 (instead of 3/5) to give Cascade earlier ROI signals.

I'll draft the two short redline passages for legal to review.

-Marissa
Head of Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Contract unwind options — exec approval ask

Laura — can you and execs weigh in? Cascade is a fast-growing regional health system; this is a $420k TCV if they convert. Marissa recommends Option A as the standard customer-friendly compromise but legal sign-off required on the specific wording to ensure we don't create an open-ended credit liability.

If we go Option A (downsell credit): sample language to review (drafted by Marissa):
"If Customer reduces committed usage tier during the six (6) month Pilot, Redwood will convert any remaining prepaid commitment to a Downsizing Credit which will be applied to subsequent invoices at the lower tier rate over a subsequent three (3) month period. The aggregate value of such Credits shall not exceed fifty percent (50%) of the remaining Prepaid Commitment."

If Option B (flat fee):
"Customer may terminate Pilot with ninety (90) days' written notice. Termination exposure shall be capped at the lesser of (i) two (2) months of the then-current monthly committed spend or (ii) 50% of remaining prepaid commitment."

Rishi
VP Sales — East
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_terms.docx (stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract unwind options — exec approval ask

Thanks for the context. I've reviewed both variants. Legal is comfortable with Option A as long as we add the following guardrails:
1) Clearly define "Committed Usage Tier" and include an objective usage measurement (30-day rolling average tokens).
2) Set Credit Duration to no more than 3 months and require credits to be consumed only against subscription/usage fees (no refunds or third-party pass-throughs).
3) Put a 12-month lookback cap so Credits cannot be created for reductions beyond the first year of the contract.

Option B is acceptable as an exec concession but request that Finance sign off on the exact cap math; I do not want ambiguous language around "50% of remaining prepaid commitment" without a precise formula.

Conditional approval: Legal signs off on Option A with the guardrails above; Option B may be used only with VP-level written approval and explicit discount routing in Deal Desk.

I'll prepare the redlined clause and send to Sean to share with Cascade.

-Laura
Chief Legal Officer
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract terms — staged ramp + unwind options

Alyssa — thanks for the patience. Appreciate the clear ask from procurement. We discussed internally and have an approved path forward:

1) Default: Option A (Downsell Credit) with guardrails: objective definition of Committed Usage Tier (30-day rolling average), credit duration capped at 3 months, credits apply only to future Redwood subscription/usage invoices, credit creation limited to changes within the first 12 months.

2) Alternative (negotiable): Option B (Flat Uncoupling Fee) may be available for enterprise-level commitments only, capped at two months of committed spend. Use of Option B requires VP-level signoff and will be noted in the Deal Desk record.

3) Revised ramp schedule: Month 1 baseline -> Month 2 step-up -> Month 4 step-up. We'll include explicit month-by-month pricing table in the SOW.

I've attached the redline with the exact clause language. If this aligns, please confirm and we'll route the final documents to DocuSign. If Cascade prefers the flat fee path, let me know and I'll request written approval from Rishi for the exception.

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_terms.docx (sent), cascade_contract_draft_v2.pdf (sent)
